source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség — Tagok (member list) and annual Fintech Report
why_relevant: Directory of the Hungarian fintech population (startups through mature firms, incubators, accelerators) plus a board roster naming affiliated companies (Barion, BlockBen, Tőkeportál, HOLD, Ergománia). The annual English-language Fintech Report doubles as a regulatory-change survey of the ecosystem.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség (Hungarian Leasing Association)
why_relevant: Interest body of asset-financing firms (leasing companies, banks, financial enterprises), founded 1991, ~36 members. Publishes market statistics and comments on financing/consumer-credit regulation; also an associate member of the Banking Association, so it sits inside the bank lobbying structure.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség — Fogalomtár (glossary)
why_relevant: A maintained Hungarian-language glossary of financing and payments terms (e.g. pénzforgalmi szolgáltatás, pénzforgalmi szolgáltató). Directly useful for building the local-language query vocabulary that the rest of the collection depends on.

source_name: Pénzügyi Vállalkozások Országos Egyesülete (PVOE)
why_relevant: Interest-representation body of non-bank financial enterprises (pénzügyi vállalkozások) — the lender population outside the credit-institution perimeter. An associate member of the Banking Association since 2017 with a cooperation agreement on shaping the legal/regulatory environment, so its statements reveal the non-bank lending lobby's asks.

source_name: Magyar Faktoring Szövetség (Hungarian Factoring Association)
why_relevant: Self-regulatory/interest body for factoring providers; publishes quarterly market volumes that the trade press picks up, and speaks for receivables-finance firms on credit and enforcement regulation. Has a LEI, so it is a formally registered legal entity traceable in GLEIF.

source_name: MABISZ — Magyar Biztosítók Szövetsége (Association of Hungarian Insurance Companies)
why_relevant: The insurance-side self-regulatory body. Explicitly states it comments on every draft law and supervisory instrument (e.g. it responded to MNB's draft recommendation on conflicts of interest for IBIP products and to a decree draft on quality-assurance calls). Its statutes even require publishing the dissenting minority view — unusually revealing about internal industry splits.

source_name: MKIK — Magyar Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara (Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry)
why_relevant: Statutory chamber that reviews national economic draft legislation and forms positions from county chambers' input; provides mandatory free advisory services on financial, tax and credit-access matters and sits on nationally mandated councils. A chamber position is the broad-business counterweight to the bank/fintech lobbies.

source_name: VOSZ — Vállalkozók és Munkáltatók Országos Szövetsége
why_relevant: National employers'/entrepreneurs' confederation that participates in tripartite consultation on economic legislation. Relevant to this cell as a demand-side voice on SME finance, cash/card acceptance and payment-cost regulation rather than as a financial-sector body.

source_name: HVCA — Magyar Kockázati- és Magántőke Egyesület (Hungarian Private Equity and Venture Capital Association)
why_relevant: ~70-member association of VC/PE investors plus legal, advisory and financial-services firms, with a browsable member directory by category. Both a pointer to the fintech-investor population and an occasional commenter on fund/investment regulation.

source_name: FinTechZone — Szabályozás (regulation) category
why_relevant: Hungarian fintech trade outlet that reports association activity, working-group launches and regulatory drafts, often quoting association officials. Frequently the only public record of what an association said during a consultation.

source_name: Fintech.hu — Szabályozás (regulation) category
why_relevant: Second Hungarian fintech outlet with a dedicated Magyar Fintech Szövetség tag page, reporting new association working groups and regulatory turns (e.g. shifts in Hungarian crypto rules). Useful as a tag-based tracker of association activity.

source_name: Portfolio.hu — 'magyar lízingszövetség' / 'lízingszövetség' tag pages
why_relevant: Tag-based aggregation of everything the leading Hungarian business outlet writes about a named association — a cheap way to catch association statements, statistics releases and consultation positions that never get a dedicated page on the association's own site.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — Wikipédia entry (HU)
why_relevant: Cheap orientation layer: official name, founding, mandate wording, historical member changes (e.g. the National Savings Cooperatives Federation's 2008-2018 membership) and outbound links. Use only to generate leads and terminology, never as an authority.

source_name: Kovács Levente: 'A Magyar Bankszövetség első három évtizede' (association history paper)
why_relevant: Written by the association's own secretary-general; documents the membership structure over time, which affiliated interest bodies joined when (PVOE from 2017, cooperation agreements on shaping the legal environment), and how the self-regulatory apparatus was built. Best single background text for interpreting the association's institutional position.

source_name: MNB Innovation Hub / FinTech Jogtár (regulatory-dialogue interface used by associations)
why_relevant: The supervisor's formal channel for dialogue with fintech firms and their associations, plus a curated FinTech legal register (Jogtár). Belongs to the supervisor rather than to industry, but is where association-side regulatory asks surface as guidance and where the fintech association's counterparties are named.

source_name: KPMG Hungary – Financial Risk & Regulation news (Pénzügyi kockázatkezelés és szabályozás hírek)
why_relevant: KPMG Hungary's dedicated FRR desk publishes a monthly regulatory digest for credit institutions, investment service providers and insurers, summarising MNB, EBA/ESMA/EIOPA and EU instruments with effective dates. It is the single most systematic Big Four regulatory-calendar product for the Hungarian financial sector and exists in parallel HU/EN versions with sub-pages per sector (e.g. 'Hitelintézetek').

source_name: KPMG Hungary corporate blog (blog.kpmg.hu)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language KPMG blog carrying dated interpretive posts on MNB recommendations, Hpt. amendments, AML/AMLA, ESG and treasury/banking topics — e.g. a March 2026 post on the MNB's new sustainability recommendation and the Hpt. amendment. Confirmed live with dated 2026 posts; often earlier and more granular than the formal newsletter.

source_name: Deloitte Legal Hungary – Hírlevelek, sajtóközlemények (newsletters/press releases)
why_relevant: Deloitte Legal (Göndöcz és Társai) publishes dated Hungarian legal newsletters; its banking/finance practice page explicitly lists AML, PSD2, MiFID, SFDR, CRR compliance and MNB recommendation compliance as service lines, so its alerts track exactly the obligation set in scope.

source_name: PwC Hungary – Kiadványok (publications) and press room
why_relevant: PwC Hungary's publications hub aggregates dated Hungarian-language analyses; its financial-sector page covers IFRS 9, sector-specific tax obligations and financial-sector regulation. Useful as a second Big Four cross-check on deadline interpretation.

source_name: Réti, Várszegi és Társai Ügyvédi Iroda (PwC Legal Hungary)
why_relevant: PwC's Hungarian member law firm, Legal 500 EMEA 2026 Top Tier, advising financial institutions. Its bilingual site is the legal-alert channel behind PwC Hungary's regulatory commentary; useful for obligations that PwC frames as legal rather than advisory content.

source_name: CMS Hungary – Legal updates (cms.law/en/hun)
why_relevant: CMS Budapest is Band 1 for Hungarian banking & finance and publishes dated English legal updates on Hungarian financial regulation ahead of official English texts — e.g. an update on Hungary proposing to widen the scope of financial entities under DORA. Exactly the 'first and clearest about a Hungarian instrument, in English' pattern this cell targets.

source_name: Wolf Theiss – Insights (Hungary banking & finance)
why_relevant: Wolf Theiss Budapest publishes bilingual client alerts on Hungarian financial regulation — confirmed recent items on Hungary's new non-performing loans rules (published in both English and Hungarian) and on factoring as a regulatory challenge. Also authors the Hungary chapter of Lexology In-Depth: Consumer Finance Law, giving a periodic structured baseline of the regime.

source_name: Schoenherr Hetényi Ügyvédi Iroda – Hungary publications
why_relevant: Schoenherr's Budapest office produces dated alerts specifically on MNB soft law and payments — confirmed items include 'The National Bank of Hungary's new ESG guideline: a brief overview' and 'The potential of open banking and ESG in Hungary'. Strong on MNB recommendation interpretation, which is exactly the A3 supervision/soft-law layer.

source_name: Gárdos Mosonyi Tomori Ügyvédi Iroda (gmtlegal.hu) – banking law commentary
why_relevant: Hungary's most specialist independent banking/capital-markets/payments boutique (est. 1992, Chambers-ranked). Confirmed to publish dated Hungarian commentary on MNB decrees — e.g. 'Új MNB-rendelet a pénzügyi panaszkezelésről' (new MNB decree on financial complaint handling). Deep, HU-first, and covers pénzforgalom (payments) instruments that international firms skip. Also a securitisation comparative-guide author.

source_name: Lakatos, Köves és Társai Ügyvédi Iroda – Híreink (news)
why_relevant: Top-ranked independent Hungarian firm (Lex Mundi member; Legal 500 2024 top-ranked in Banking & Capital Markets). Its bilingual news feed carries client alerts on financial-sector legislation; the /news path is a clean, crawlable listing.

source_name: Oppenheim Ügyvédi Iroda – banking & financial sector
why_relevant: Leading Budapest firm whose banking practice explicitly covers banking/financial regulatory advice, AML/CFT compliance and licensing (engedélyezés). A likely publisher of dated alerts on AML and authorisation obligations; the practice and sector pages are the entry points.

source_name: Andrékó Ferenczi Kinstellar Ügyvédi Iroda – Hungary insights
why_relevant: Band 1 Hungarian banking & finance practice (IFLR1000/Chambers) inside a CEE-wide firm that publishes regular jurisdiction-tagged legal updates. Valuable for CEE-comparative framing of Hungarian implementation timing.
